𝗟𝗮𝘂𝗻𝗰𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗻 𝗔𝗜 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗶𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗮𝗺𝗲 𝗮𝘀 𝗰𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝘁𝗯𝗼𝘁.

A chatbot answers inside an interface.

An agent needs a model, instructions, identity, tools, distribution and an economic layer.

AINFT Nova brings those components into one launch environment.

Its structure can be understood through four connected layers:

Agent Creation → Autonomous Identity → Social Execution → Token Economy

The first layer is agent creation.

A user begins by defining what the agent is supposed to do.

That includes its purpose, behavioural instructions, communication style and assigned tasks.

One agent may be built for research.

Another may focus on community engagement.

Another may publish market updates or coordinate activities around an ecosystem.

The model supplies general intelligence, but the configuration gives that intelligence a job.

Without clear instructions, the agent is only a model endpoint.

With an assigned role, operating rules and the required tools, it becomes a specialised digital worker.

The second layer is autonomous digital identity.

An agent needs more than a name and profile image.

It needs an identity that persists across interactions.

That identity connects its public presence, behaviour, history and ownership structure.

It allows users to recognise the same agent over time instead of treating every response as an isolated session.

This matters because reputation cannot develop without continuity.

An agent that publishes useful information and responds consistently begins creating an observable track record.

Its identity becomes the container for that record.

The third layer is execution.

An AI agent becomes useful when it moves beyond generating text and performs defined actions.

For a social agent, that may include creating content, responding to users and maintaining an active presence.

For a research agent, it may involve gathering information and delivering structured outputs.

The intelligence comes from the model.

The operating logic determines when and how that intelligence is used.

Nova connects the agent’s intelligence to the environment where it is expected to operate.

This is where automation and autonomy separate.

Automation repeats a fixed instruction.

An autonomous agent can interpret changing input, select an appropriate response and continue operating within limits defined by its creator.

Its autonomy exists inside those rules.

The fourth layer is tokenisation.

Launching a token alongside an agent creates an economic system around the digital identity.

The token can coordinate the agent, its creator and its community.

It can make participation measurable, create an on-chain ownership layer and give the ecosystem a transferable economic component.

But a token does not automatically make an agent useful.

The order matters.

First, the agent needs a clear purpose.

Then it needs consistent execution.

After that, a token can organise participation around the value the agent produces.

Without utility, the token is detached from the agent.

Without an economic layer, a useful agent may lack a native mechanism for coordinating its community.

Nova brings both sides into one launch process.

The complete system looks like this:

A creator defines the agent.

⬇️

The model provides reasoning and generation.

⬇️

The configuration gives it boundaries.

⬇️

Its identity gives it continuity.

⬇️

Its social layer gives it distribution.

⬇️

Its activity creates a public record.

⬇️

Its token adds an on-chain economy around that activity.

Users can then interact not only with an AI response, but with a persistent digital entity that can communicate, build recognition and support a community-linked economy.

That is the larger purpose of AINFT Nova.

It reduces the distance between having an agent idea and launching an operational agent ecosystem.

The user is not merely creating a bot.

They are assembling intelligence, identity, distribution and tokenisation into one product.

This also changes what “launching” means.

A traditional token launch begins with an asset and attempts to build attention around it.

An agent launch can begin with behaviour.

The agent communicates.

The community observes.

Its usefulness becomes visible.

The token economy can then develop around an active digital identity rather than an empty symbol.

The strongest agents will not succeed because they speak the most.

They will succeed because their identity remains consistent, their actions remain useful and their economic layer stays connected to real participation.

AINFT Nova is building the launch infrastructure for that transition:

From models to agents.

From sessions to identities.

From audiences to communities.

From attention to programmable economies.

Not another chatbot window.

A system for launching digital entities that can think, act, persist and coordinate value.

Explore AINFT Nova. 🤖

Thrilled to see the @AppliedSciAI literature agent win the Best AI Scientist award at one of the world's leading ML conferences 🤯

You can try the agent in the link below.

Some of its killer features come from the insight that the signals that often matter most in a scientific paper aren't in the text - they're scattered across figures, tables, gels, micrographs and electrophysiology traces.

It was inspiring to watch @lukasweidener @markoasi1 & @mihailoxyz attack this problem and build an agent that hit SOTA across major literature search benchmarks like LitQA3, FigQA2 & TableQA2. 

ASI is focused on cardiac risk, using model-assay loops to build a “virtual heart” that predicts cardiac safety for small molecules, guides lead optimization and could eventually power digital twins in clinical trials. Our team runs the agent for internal R&D and to generate training data for our cardiac safety models.

Concrete case: when CardioSafe flags a compound as toxic and its RL mode proposes safer analogs, the literature agent checks whether anyone has already assayed a close neighbor - so we’re not spending months on a "safer" molecule someone else quietly killed years ago.

That answer almost never lives in the text of a paper, rather it’s usually in a dose-response curve, summplementary assay table or ion-channel panel buried in a figure. It's a good example of how prediction models paired with scientific reasoning creates new capabilities in drug discovery.

Try ASI’s literature agent + CardioSafe today: https://t.co/r7HFewNhIA

#Lenskart has quietly built one of India's strongest retail franchises.

A few key takeaways from BofA's initiation report:
✅ Only ~5% market share in a highly underpenetrated eyewear market

✅ 23% / 39% / 46% Revenue / EBITDA / EPS CAGR expected (FY26–FY28)

✅ AI is becoming a key competitive advantage—from remote diagnostics and virtual try-ons to personalized recommendations, store expansion and supply-chain optimisation.

✅ 2,600+ stores and 120 million+ app downloads, making it one of India's largest retail brands.

✅ Store payback period of less than 1 year, with better unit economics in smaller towns.

✅ International business is scaling well, with profitability already looking stronger than India.

✅ Healthy operating leverage could expand EBITDA margins by ~300 bps by FY28, while management aspires for ~25% long-term EBITDA margins.

✅ Strong balance sheet and healthy free cash flow generation provide ample firepower to invest in stores, technology and manufacturing.

This isn't just an eyewear retailer anymore. It's a vertically integrated, AI-enabled consumer platform with a long runway for compounding.

If execution continues, I believe Lenskart deserves to trade at a premium valuation despite looking expensive on near-term earnings.

What if your robot could remember past experiences to generate perfectly tailored training data? 

Researchers from Zhejiang Sci-Tech University and Nanjing University present EMCES: a system that uses episodic memory to guide a diffusion model, creating high-quality synthetic data for reinforcement learning. It prioritizes the most useful past moments. 

The result? Outperforms existing methods across multiple environments, boosting RL algorithm performance. 

Bonus: a hashing trick cuts storage by 8000x and time by 25.5x—without losing quality.

Episodic Memory-Guided Controllable Experience Synthesis for Reinforcement Learning

Paper: https://t.co/SmiSeY65w5

Our report: https://t.co/CtjxWVlLMj
